content: 1. Kelly E, Feng Z, Gidley M, Sinigalliano C, Kumar N, Donahue AG, et al. (2018). This study investigates the impact of beach management policies on the quality of recreational water. Published in the Journal of Environmental Management, it provides a detailed analysis of how different management strategies influence water quality parameters, with implications for public health and environmental sustainability. 2. Khan IU, Hill S, Nowak E, Edge TA (2013). This research examines the effect of incubation temperature on the detection of thermophilic Campylobacter species in freshwater beach environments, nearby wastewater effluents, and bird fecal droppings. The findings, published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, highlight the role of environmental factors in pathogen detection and public health risk assessment. 3. Kidd SE, Hagen F, Tscharke RL, Huynh M, Bartlett KH, Fyfe M, et al. (2004). This paper identifies a rare genotype of Cryptococcus gattii as the causative agent of a cryptococcosis outbreak on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, Canada. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA, it underscores the importance of molecular epidemiology in understanding fungal outbreaks. 4. Kinzelman J, Pond K, Longmaid KD, Bagley RC (2004). This study evaluates the effects of two mechanical beach grooming strategies on Escherichia coli density in beach sand at a southwestern Lake Michigan beach. Published in Aquatic Ecosystem Health and Management, it provides insights into the relationship between beach maintenance practices and microbial contamination. 5. Lamparelli CC, Pogreba-Brown K, Verhougstraete M, Sato MIZ, de Castro Bruni A, Wade TJ, et al. (2015). This cohort study, conducted in Brazil, questions the appropriateness of fecal indicator bacteria as measures of recreational water risks in tropical environments. Published in Water Research, it emphasizes the need for region-specific risk assessment tools. 6. León-López CE, Arreola-Lizárraga JA, Padilla-Arredondo G, Chávez-Villalba JE, Mendoza-Salgado RA, Méndez-Rodríguez LC, et al. (2018). This research explores the temporal variability of enterococci and their associated sources at three subtropical recreational beaches. Published in Oceanological and Hydrobiological Studies, it provides valuable data on microbial dynamics in coastal environments. 7. Llewellyn PJ, Shackley SE (1996). This study investigates the effects of mechanical beach-cleaning on invertebrate populations. Published in British Wildlife, it highlights the ecological consequences of beach maintenance practices. 8. Male O (1990). This chapter discusses the significance of mycology in medicine, emphasizing the clinical and environmental importance of fungi. It is included in the book Frontiers in Mycology, edited by Hawksworth DL and published by CAB International. 9. Mann P (2010). This PowerPoint presentation, prepared by the Miami-Dade County Health Department, addresses feline hookworms and their role in human cutaneous larva migrans, providing a comprehensive overview of zoonotic risks. 10. Maziarz EK, Perfect JR (2016). This article, published in Infectious Disease Clinics of North America, provides an in-depth review of cryptococcosis, including its epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and management strategies. 11. Mendes B, Urbano P, Alves C, Morais J, Lapa N, Oliveira JS (1998). This study evaluates fungi as environmental microbiological indicators, with findings published in Water Science and Technology. It highlights the role of fungi in monitoring environmental health. 12. Miceli A, Krishnamurthy K (2019). This entry on blastomycosis, available on the StatPearls website, provides a detailed overview of the fungal infection, including its pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and treatment options. 13. Ministry of Health of the Republic of Lithuania (2007). This document outlines public health guidelines and policies, emphasizing the importance of environmental health monitoring. 14. Monteiro S, Brondani G, Brandão J, Santos R (2016). Presented at the Fifth Food and Environmental Virology Congress in Kusatsu, Japan, this study examines the presence of viruses in beach sand, highlighting potential public health risks. 15. Nestor I, Costin-Lazar L, Sovrea D, Ionescu N (1984). This research, published in Zentralblatt Bakteriologie Mikrobiologie Hygiene B, focuses on the detection of enteroviruses in seawater and beach sand, providing insights into viral contamination in coastal environments. 16. Oshiro R, Fujioka R (1995). This study identifies sand, soil, and pigeon droppings as sources of indicator bacteria in the waters of Hanauma Bay, Oahu, Hawaii. Published in Water Science and Technology, it underscores the importance of source tracking in water quality management. 17. Papadakis JA, Mavridou A, Richardson SC, Lampiri M, Marcelou U (1997). This research, published in Water Research, investigates bather-related microbial and yeast populations in sand and seawater, providing data on human impact on beach environments. 18. Pianetti A, Bruscolini F, Sabatini L, Colantoni P (2004). This preliminary study, published in the Journal of Applied Microbiology, characterizes microbial populations in marine sediments from bathing areas along the Pesaro-Gabicce coast in Italy. 19. Phillips MC, Solo-Gabriele HM, Piggot AM, Klaus JS, Zhang Y (2011). This study, published in Water Research, explores the relationships between sand and water quality at recreational beaches, emphasizing the interconnectedness of these environments. 20. Piggot AM, Klaus JS, Johnson S, Phillips MC, Solo-Gabriele HM (2012). Published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, this research examines the relationship between enterococcal levels and sediment biofilms at recreational beaches in South Florida. 21. Plano LR, Garza AC, Shibata T, Elmir SM, Kish J, Sinigalliano CD, et al. (2011). This study, published in BMC Microbiology, investigates the shedding of Staphylococcus aureus and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) from bathers in marine waters. 22. Plano LRW, Shibata T, Garza AC, Kish J, Fleisher J, Sinigalliano CD, et al. (2013). This research, published in Microbial Ecology, identifies human-associated MRSA in a subtropical recreational marine beach, highlighting the public health implications of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. 23. Praveena SM, Shamira SS, Ismail SNS, Aris AZ (2016). This study, published in Marine Pollution Bulletin, provides baseline findings on fecal indicator bacteria in tropical beach sand along the Port Dickson coastline, Strait of Malacca, Malaysia. 24. Roca MA, Brown R, Solo-Gabriele HM (2019). Published in Marine Pollution Bulletin, this study examines fecal indicator bacteria levels at beaches in the Florida Keys following Hurricane Irma, providing insights into the impact of natural disasters on water quality. 25. Roses Codinachs M, Isern Vins AM, Ferrer Escobar MD, Fernandez Perez F (1988). This research, published in Revista Sanidad Higiene Publica, investigates microbiological contamination of sand from Barcelona city beaches, emphasizing urban impacts on coastal environments. 26. Sabino R, Veríssimo C, Cunha MA, Wergikoski B, Ferreira FC, Rodrigues R, et al. (2011). This study, published in Marine Pollution Bulletin, highlights the unacknowledged risk of pathogenic fungi at coastal resorts, with a focus on microbial sand quality in Portugal. 27. Sabino R, Rodrigues R, Costa I, Carneiro C, Cunha M, Duarte A, et al. (2014). Published in Science of the Total Environment, this research emphasizes the importance of routine screening for harmful microorganisms in beach sands and its implications for public health. 28. Schets FM, Schijven JF, de Roda Husman AM (2011). This study, published in Water Research, assesses exposure risks for swimmers in bathing waters and swimming pools, providing a framework for risk management. 29. Schöttler G (1998). This study, published in Gesundheitswesen, investigates the incidence of Toxocara ova, particularly those associated with visceral larva migrans, in beach sand from Warnemünde, Germany. 30. Shah AH, Abdelzaher AM, Phillips M, Hernandez R, Solo-Gabriele HM, Kish J, et al. (2011). Published in the Journal of Applied Microbiology, this research correlates indicator microbes with pathogenic bacteria, yeasts, and helminths in sand at a subtropical recreational beach site. 31. Shatti JA, Abdullah THA (1999). This study, published in Water Science and Technology, examines marine pollution caused by wastewater discharge in Kuwait, highlighting the environmental and public health implications. 32. Shibata T, Solo-Gabriele HM (2012). This study, published in Environmental Science and Technology, conducts a quantitative microbial risk assessment of human illness from exposure to marine beach sand. 33. Signorile G, Montagna MT, Sena G, Cavallo RA (1992). This bacteriological survey, published in L’Igiene Moderna, investigates water and sand quality in the Taranto coastal areas, providing data on microbial contamination. 34. Silva PF, Cavalcanti IM, Irmão JI, Rocha FJ (2009). Published in Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de São Paulo, this study examines common beach sand contamination due to enteroparasites on the southern coast of Pernambuco State, Brazil. 35. Soge OO, Meschke JS, No DB, Roberts MC (2009). This study, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, characterizes methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species isolated from public marine beaches on the US west coast. 36. Solo-Gabriele H, Harwood V, Kay D, Fujioka R, Sadowsky M, Whitman R, et al. (2016). Published in the Journal of Marine Biology Association UK, this study discusses the potential for infectious disease transmission through beach sand and provides recommendations for public health. 37. Sousa MLR (1990). This publication, issued by the National Institute of Health in Lisbon, addresses fungal infections (mycoses) and their epidemiological significance. 38. Sow D, Soro F, Javelle E, Simon F, Parola P, Gautret P (2017). Published in Travel Medicine and Infectious Disease, this study profiles the epidemiology of cutaneous larva migrans in travelers returning to France between 2003 and 2015. 39. Suzuki Y, Teranishi K, Matsuwaki T, Nukazawa K, Ogura Y (2018). This study, published in Science of the Total Environment, examines bacterial pollution caused by a strong typhoon event and the subsequent restoration of a recreational beach, focusing on transitions in fecal bacterial counts and bacterial flora in beach sand. 40. Tanaka RJ, Boon NJ, Vrcelj K, Nguyen A, Vinci C, Armstrong-James D, et al. (2015). Published in Scientific Reports, this in silico modeling study reveals fungal persistence following low-dose spore inhalation, providing insights into fungal exposure risks. 41. Thapaliya D, Hellwig EJ, Kadariya J, Grenier D, Jefferson AJ, Dalman M (2017). Published in GeoHealth, this study investigates the prevalence and characterization of Staphylococcus aureus and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus on public recreational beaches in northeast Ohio. 42. Tugrul-Icemer G, Topaloglu A (2011). This study, published in the Journal of Coastal Research, examines the levels of yeast, mold, and Pseudomonas species in Antalya beaches, providing data on microbial contamination. 43. Tyner EH, Jensen P, Ngochera M, Bootsma HA (2018). Published in the Journal of Great Lakes Research, this study investigates the distribution of Escherichia coli in the nearshore zone of Lake Malawi, highlighting the dynamics of microbial contamination. 44. USEPA (United States Environmental Protection Agency) (2011). The Exposure Factors Handbook, published by the National Center for Environmental Assessment, provides comprehensive data on exposure factors relevant to environmental health risk assessments. 45. Van Wijnen JH, Clausing P, Brunekreff B (1990). Published in Environmental Research, this study estimates soil ingestion by children, providing data critical for assessing exposure to soil contaminants. 46. Vieira RHSF, Rodrigues DP, Menezes EA, Evangelista NSS, Reis EMF, Barreto LP, et al. (2001). This study, published in the Brazilian Journal of Microbiology, investigates microbial contamination of sand from major beaches in Fortaleza, Ceará State, Brazil. 47. Viji R, Shrinithivihahshini ND, Santhanam P, Balakrishnan S, Yi Y, Rajivgandhi G (2019). Published in Marine Pollution Bulletin, this study conducts biomonitoring of environmental indicators and pathogenic microorganisms at pilgrimage beaches along the Bay of Bengal, southeast coast of India. 48. Villacampa Y, López I, Aragonés L, García C, López M, Palazón A (2017). Published in the International Journal of Sustainable Development and Planning, this study compares water quality at urban and non-urban beach environments. 49. Vogel LJ, O’Carroll DM, Edge TA, Robinson CE (2016). Published in Environmental Science and Technology, this study examines the release of Escherichia coli from foreshore sand and pore water during intensified wave conditions at a recreational beach. 50. Warris A, Klaassen CHW, Meis JFGM, De Ruiter MT, De Valk HA, Abrahamsen TG, et al. (2003). Published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology, this study uses molecular epidemiology to analyze Aspergillus fumigatus isolates from water, air, and patients, identifying two clusters of genetically distinct strains. 51. Weiskerger CJ, Brandão J, Ahmed W, Aslan A, Avolio L, Badgley BD, et al. (2019). Published in Water Research, this study explores the impacts of a changing earth on microbial dynamics and human health risks in the continuum between beach water and sand. 52. Whiley H, Austin J, da Silva GM, Ross K (2018). Published in the Journal of Coastal Research, this study investigates the presence of fecal indicator bacteria in sand at South Port Beach, South Australia. 53. Whitman RL, Nevers MB, Byappanahalli MN (2006). Published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, this study examines the watershed-wide distribution of Escherichia coli along southern Lake Michigan, using an integrated approach. 54. Whitman RL, Harwood VJ, Edge TA, Nevers M, Byappanahalli M, Vijayavel K, et al. (2014). This review, published in Reviews in Environmental Science and Biotechnology, integrates environmental, ecological, and public health perspectives on microbes in beach sands. 55. Wu MZ, O’Carroll DM, Vogel LJ, Robinson CE (2017). Published in Environmental Science and Technology, this study investigates the effect of low-energy waves on the accumulation and transport of fecal indicator bacteria in sand and pore water at freshwater beaches. 56. Yamahara KM, Sassoubre LM, Goodwin KD, Boehm AB (2012). Published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, this study examines the occurrence and persistence of bacterial pathogens and indicator organisms in beach sand along the California coast. 57. Zanoli Sato MI, Di Bari M, Lamparelli CC, Truzzi AC, Coelho MCLS, Hachich EM (2005). Published in the Brazilian Journal of Microbiology, this study evaluates the sanitary quality of sands from marine recreational beaches in São Paulo, Brazil. These rewritten descriptions maintain the integrity of the original references while presenting the information in a clear, professional, and accessible manner for medical and scientific audiences.
